title: LlamaParse Pricing: Plans, Credits & Costs (2026)
summary: LlamaParse pricing covers free, starter, and pro tiers with different usage limits and costs.
body_markdown:
## Automate the file-to-parser step with Activepieces


Do not expect Activepieces to make LlamaParse cheaper.


It can keep documents that don't need parsing from spending credits, and a run costs 1 credit on Activepieces however many steps the filter adds, which matters when you can't yet say what Reducto or Mistral OCR would charge for the same pile.


### Where an automation fits around a parser


Think of Activepieces as a workflow automation tool: you chain a trigger to a series of steps, and it runs them each time the trigger fires. It sits around the parser, not inside it.


Its core is MIT-licensed, and its 747 integrations are the ones in the` packages/pieces/community` directory of the open-source monorepo on GitHub, counted there rather than quoted from a marketing page, so the count is auditable.


Nothing in Activepieces alters the per-page or per-credit rate, which's set by whichever LlamaParse mode your documents force: 1 credit a page on Fast, 4 on layout mode.


So price the retainer on the parsing mode first, then treat the automation as the thing that decides how many files reach it.


For a client who sends documents by email or drops them in a folder, that matters on the invoice.


If handling's manual, someone on your team uploads files and pastes results, and that time lands on your side unless you bill for it. A flow replaces that labor and gives you a consistent run you can count and attribute to a single client.


Four steps, in this order:


1. Trigger on a new file or a new email attachment.
2. Filter out anything that isn't a PDF, and anything already processed.
3. Call the LlamaParse API through an HTTP step.
4. Write the parsed result to a Google Sheet.


Nothing is charged until the HTTP step, which is where credits are spent. Everything before it's free of parsing charges, which's why the order matters: steps one and two are your only chance to stop a wasted call.


### Filtering files to avoid wasting LlamaParse credits


Put the filter before the HTTP step, never after it. A non-PDF that reaches LlamaParse either fails or gets parsed in a way the client didn't ask for, and you may pay for the attempt either way.


Checking the file type up front removes that risk at no cost.


Clients resend the same attachment, forward a thread twice, or re-upload a corrected file with the original still in the folder. Each repeat parsed again's a charge nobody agreed to. Those duplicates are the quieter leak.


If the flow records each processed file in the Google Sheet, the filter can check that record first and stop a repeat before it costs anything.


That also keeps a shared account honest. One client's resend habit shouldn't be absorbed by the credits you're carrying for everyone else.


Activepieces is the better fit for teams that need to control how many files reach a document parser, judged on whether the automation layer can be verified and priced predictably.


It does not lower LlamaParse's per-page rate, which the parsing mode sets, but its 747 integrations are counted directly from the open-source monorepo rather than taken from a marketing page, and a run costs 1 credit however many filter steps it adds.


For a buyer who can't yet say what Reducto or Mistral OCR would charge for the same pile, that auditable catalogue and flat run cost make it the safer thing to build around.
